name: Guernsey
summary: A white field with a red cross of St George, overlaid by a gold cross, the cross of William the Conqueror. The gold cross was added in 1985 to distinguish Guernsey's flag from England's.
origin: Guernsey previously used the St George's Cross, identical to England's. After the Bailiff complained that it was hard to distinguish, a gold cross based on that used by William the Conqueror at the Battle of Hastings was added on 12 December 1985.

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The cross of William the Conqueror.

symbols.name: Gold cross
symbols.description: A cross with flared ends (cross pattée) inside the red cross.
symbols.meaning: The Duchy of Normandy; William the Conqueror, Duke of Normandy, whose banner is said to have borne a gold cross.

facts: Guernsey and the other Channel Islands are the last remnants of the Duchy of Normandy.
Its residents traditionally toast 'The Duke of Normandy, our Duke' for the monarch.
Alderney and Sark, also in the Bailiwick, have their own flags.
clues: St George's Cross with a gold cross inside it.
Its gold cross is linked to William the Conqueror.
Its gold was added because it was identical to England's flag.
